The goal of credit scoring is to predict whether someone will pay their debts, and who they'll pay them to.  The more debts a person has, and the less money they pay back on those debts, the better they'll be.  Most credit scoring models have a minimum debt to income ratio (the ratio of how much debt a person owes vs. how much income they make), and most models will exclude some debt types (overtime, child support, alimony/ spousal support, taxes, payments to a garnishing creditor, student loans, medical bills, utility bills/ service charges, credit card payments, mortgage payment, certain types of bankruptcy, taxes that have been paid off, and fees paid to a collection agency).
